introduction: Michigan weatherization provides no-cost energy-conservation services for qualifying households. Local Community Action Agencies handle applications.
description: Michigan weatherization provides no-cost energy-conservation services for qualifying households. Local Community Action Agencies handle applications.

sections.who: Homeowners and renters must meet financial and property conditions. The home must be occupied and suitable for the work; homes undergoing remodeling, in foreclosure or for sale do not qualify under the listed conditions.
sections.get: An audit determines appropriate efficiency measures. Weatherization is not general rehabilitation, and no individual upgrade is guaranteed.
sections.docs:
• Household income evidence.
  • Homeownership evidence or landlord permission.
  • Utility-company information and recent gas and electric bills.
sections.apply:
1. Find the local agency

    Use the Community Action Agency link on Seeking Weatherization Services.

  2. Submit intake records

    Confirm the agency’s application and property checklist.

  3. Arrange the energy audit

    The assessment decides whether the home is ready and which measures fit.
sections.after: Ask about waiting times and repairs outside the program’s scope before planning installation.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using Michigan WAP applicant guidance. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: No. Measures depend on the audit.
Does it repair every unsafe condition?
No. Work must fit weatherization’s scope.
Are recently weatherized homes served again?
The state excludes homes served within the past 15 years.
